answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying transaction size to an earned, non-transferable record of completed exchanges. A new identity starts with a tiny haven for small trades only, and its limit grows solely as it completes exchanges with distinct partners over time, like a river widening only where real flow has passed. Credit cannot be bought, transferred, or copied, and a prism of past trades is publicly visible for every identity, so an attacker creating many fakes gains only many tiny limits, and each fake must separately earn its own history.
